title: WHEN CHILDREN WALK IN A LAND OF SHADOWS

sense.text:
This comes in the middle of the factors that lead and follow troubled children into adulthood: unstable housing, homelessness and poverty, food insecurity, highly unbalanced eating and excessive processed food (Twinkies, potato chips, Oreos, Takis; a fourteen-year-old weighing 200 pounds has a problem), sleep deprivation from abuse, arguing and fighting at home or from a child left on the internet all night, social isolation where nobody ever tells the child good job, well done, you are kind, you are smart, you are important, constant moving from school to school, chronic sickness, and persistent discrimination, racism and persecution out in the world. Your child does not dictate what they eat and when they eat. You as the parent dictate that.

Then behavioral problems punished harshly instead of being treated with support. Some things can be handled by taking away the laptop, or a pop on the hand or a pop on the thigh while they are young. Some of your kids are just bad, no good, and you have to be aware of your own child.

“Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.” The key words are “should go.” You train the child in the way he should go, but as they get older, become teenagers and become adults at 20, some will make their own decision and say they do not want to follow that way. That is their decision.

“Even a child is known by his doings, whether his work be pure, and whether it be right.” You know your child by the things they do. If you know your daughter likes to go in men’s faces and shake her butt, you know she is going to be a hoe; she has hoe tendencies already, from something she saw on the internet or saw you doing, mama. If your son goes around trying to fight every child he meets and taking their toys, he is a bully, brother, and it ain’t cute. If your child is prone to lie, you know that child is going to grow up and be a liar. Watching them through the years, you already see what that little girl and that boy are going to turn into.

What gets under the skin is parents who lie for their kids and make believe they did not know their daughter was a hoochie mama, or that their boy was a thief. You knew. He is stealing from you, he comes to congregation stealing, he is stealing at school. You saw all the signs, and people have told you and complained to you about your child, and you act like you hear nothing. A child is known by his doings.

precepts.why:
“If thy daughter be shameless, keep her in straitly.” When a daughter’s doings show she is shameless, she has to be kept in, “lest she abuse herself through overmuch liberty.” That abuse through overmuch liberty is talking about sex.

It is what happened to Dinah. She wanted to go out and see the women of the land, and they let her just walk on out there. Our forefathers were not perfect men or perfect women: they let their daughter Dinah walk around, and she got snatched up by a Hamite. The daughter known by her doings has to be kept in straitly, not given liberty.

sense.text: Having a lot of children was taught earlier, but there is a downside to that as well. “Desire not a multitude of unprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons.” Don’t delight in unprofitable children. All them boys, them girls you got, you know whether they are good or not. If they are unprofitable, don’t rejoice in them.

“Though they multiply, rejoice not in them, except the fear of the Lord be with them.” That is the only time to rejoice in a bunch of kids. If you have a lot of children and they fear the Lord, then rejoice. If they don’t fear God, don’t rejoice.

“Trust not thou in their life, neither respect their multitude”: don’t trust in their life, and don’t respect their numbers. “for one that is just is better than a thousand”: one just child, one child that keeps the commandments, is better than a thousand unprofitable kids. “and better it is to die without children, than to have them that are ungodly”: it is better to die without ever having children than to have a bunch of ungodly kids, because they are going to bring shame to you. You will be all on the news.

That is what a group of unprofitable children looks like: grown women fighting in the middle of a street in Philadelphia, more jumping in, the fight pouring into the house past a screen door with the children watching, the police coming, as that way of settling things is passed from one generation to the next. Some of your kids are just like that, especially the girls who like to fight when they don’t get their way. Unprofitable kids. Do not rejoice in children like that.

Job was a man in the land of Uz, “perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.” “And there were born unto him seven sons and three daughters”, with great substance, “so that this man was the greatest of all the men of the east.”
“And his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day”: they were celebrating birthdays. And they “sent and called for their three sisters to eat and to drink with them.”

When the days of their feasting were over, Job “sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all”, meaning ten, one for each child. “for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.”

There is something very odd about that. Job kept sending up sacrifices saying perhaps my sons have sinned. Job knew exactly what his kids were doing.

precepts.why:
“Thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking wine in their eldest brother’s house”: the same feasting of verse 4. They were celebrating a birthday.

“And, behold, there came a great wind from the wilderness, and smote the four corners of the house, and it fell upon the young men, and they are dead.” The children Job had been offering for were taken in the middle of their feasting.

Job himself says it: “I have sinned; what shall I do unto thee, O thou preserver of men? why hast thou set me as a mark against thee, so that I am a burden to myself?”

Then he prays, “why dost thou not pardon my transgression, and take away mine iniquity? for now shall I sleep in the dust; and thou shalt seek me in the morning, but I shall not be.” Job was praying, why don’t you pardon my transgression, Lord? And take away mine iniquity. Uh-oh. The man who kept sacrificing, saying perhaps my sons have sinned, says it himself: I have sinned.

Bildad the Shuhite answers Job: “How long wilt thou speak these things? and how long shall the words of thy mouth be like a strong wind? Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?” Does God do anything wrong?

Verse 4 is the point: “If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression”. Everybody knew what Job’s children were doing. That is why Job was sacrificing, but he turned a blind eye to it. Maybe they cursed God while they were drinking and getting drunk. Job knew what they were doing.

sense.text: The man went up yearly “to worship and to sacrifice unto the Lord of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the Lord, were there.” So the high priest Eli had two sons, Hophni and Phinehas.

precepts.why: Still going with bad kids. “Now the sons of Eli were sons of Belial; they knew not the Lord.” The high priest’s own sons were children of Belial, meaning wicked kids. They were wicked sons, and they were the priests of the Lord.

“Now Eli was very old, and heard all that his sons did unto all Israel”: he heard what his sons did unto all Israel, “and how they lay with the women that assembled at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.” Hophni and Phinehas were sexing the women who were coming to have their sacrifices done.

Eli said to them, “Why do ye such things? for I hear of your evil dealings by all this people. Nay, my sons; for it is no good report that I hear: ye make the Lord’s people to transgress.” The high priest heard of their evil dealings from all the people.

This is where it should have started. “Also before they burnt the fat, the priest’s servant came, and said to the man that sacrificed, Give flesh to roast for the priest; for he will not have sodden flesh of thee, but raw.”

The man bringing the sacrifice would say, “Let them not fail to burn the fat presently, and then take as much as thy soul desireth”: let me finish roasting it, let me finish cooking it, and then y’all can take as much as you desire. But the servant of Eli’s sons would answer him, “Nay; but thou shalt give it me now.”
